solutions.check: 30 entries, 60 crossings, 0 conflicts; answers matched to the grid by number, direction and length

clue.text: Language of sailor about to land in Africa

indicators.note: about signals that the short word for a sailor is turned round

parts.note: OS, ordinary seaman, is a crossword sailor
Mali is a West African country

explanation.surface: Someone asks what tongue a seaman speaks as he comes ashore in Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: Somali is the Cushitic tongue spoken in the Horn of Africa, so it is a language.

clue.text: Quarrel with mate about hot and cold chicken on grill

parts.note: a spat is a quarrel

indicators.note: about means around, so the friend word goes round the two letters

parts.note: cock is British slang for mate, a friend
H for hot, on taps
C for cold, on taps

explanation.surface: Two friends row over warm and chilled chicken on the barbecue.
explanation.walkthrough: COCK ('mate', old London slang for pal) goes round H and C to give CHCOCK.
explanation.definitionFit: A spatchcock is a chicken split open and flattened for grilling.

clue.text: Flyer losing. tail over old Eastern city

indicators.note: losing tail, the stop a scanning slip, means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a macaw is a parrot, a flying bird

explanation.surface: A bird drops its tail feathers above an ancient city in the East.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' puts the cut bird on top of O in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Macao, the former Portuguese territory on the south China coast, is a city of the East.

clue.text: Temptation overcoming Delius regularly in idle hours

indicators.note: overcoming is read as coming over, so the temptation word wraps round the letters

parts.note: a lure is a temptation

indicators.note: regularly means every other letter is taken

explanation.surface: The lure of Delius's music wins out in someone's spare hours.
explanation.walkthrough: 'overcoming' is read as coming over, a container; Delius was an English composer, whose name gives every second letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Leisure is free time, hours spent idle away from work.

clue.text: Boy and girl penning a short composition

indicators.note: penning means enclosing, so the boy and girl hold the single letter between them

parts.note: a boy is a son
Tina is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A young couple write a little piece of music together.
explanation.definitionFit: A sonatina is a brief, simple sonata, a short piece of music.

clue.text: Many stars having time for one dramatist

indicators.note: for means in place of, so one letter replaces another

parts.note: Orion is a constellation, many stars
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A star-studded production with time for one playwright.
explanation.walkthrough: Joe Orton was an English playwright of the 1960s.
explanation.definitionFit: Joe Orton wrote Loot and Entertaining Mr Sloane, so he was a playwright.

clue.text: Studio that is involved in later broadcast

indicators.note: involved in means placed inside the other letters
broadcast means scattered, so the letters are spread about

explanation.surface: The studio is involved in a programme to be aired later.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' looks like a radio slot in the surface, but signals the anagram of 'later'; 'involved in' is the container.
explanation.definitionFit: An atelier is an artist's or designer's workshop, i.e. a studio.

clue.text: Rash of offensive books by current politician

parts.note: I is the symbol for electric current
MP is Member of Parliament
rude means offensive
NT is New Testament, books of the Bible

explanation.surface: An outbreak of rude writing comes from a sitting MP.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rash' looks like a skin complaint but is the adjective meaning reckless.
explanation.definitionFit: Rash means hasty and unwise, so an imprudent act is a rash one.

clue.text: Marry Charlie he has no wife

indicators.note: has no means the letter is taken away

parts.note: a charlie and a wally are both British slang for a fool

explanation.surface: Charlie is told to get married since he is still single.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Charlie' looks like a name, but both 'charlie' and 'wally' are British slang for a fool.
explanation.definitionFit: To ally is to join in union, as marriage joins two people or houses.

clue.text: Minister's given up opening wine

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the word reads upwards, so backwards

parts.note: Rev, Reverend, is the title of a minister
a mouth is an opening

explanation.surface: A clergyman has given up opening the wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'given up' looks like abstaining, but 'up' turns REV over to VER.
explanation.definitionFit: Vermouth is a fortified white wine flavoured with herbs.

clue.text: Author and I chatter about gripping chapter

indicators.note: gripping means holding inside, so the abbreviation is placed within the mix
about here means around or in disarray, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A writer and the speaker gossip over a gripping section of a book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' tells you to rearrange I and CHATTER; 'gripping' then has that mix hold C.
explanation.definitionFit: An architect is the author or originator of a plan or scheme, as in the architect of reform.

clue.text: Banish former Tory leader half heartedly

parts.note: ex means former

indicators.note: half of the doubled middle letters of the name is dropped, so the heart is only half there

parts.note: Sir Robert Peel was a Conservative Prime Minister

explanation.surface: Throw out an old Conservative chief without much enthusiasm.
explanation.walkthrough: Robert Peel led the Tories in the 1830s and 1840s; his name's heart is EE, and half of it goes.
explanation.definitionFit: To expel someone is to drive them out, which is to banish them.

clue.text: French snack from menu or course I fancy? Without question!

indicators.note: without in its old sense means outside, so the jumbled letters go round the abbreviation
fancy as an adjective means elaborate, telling you to rework these letters

explanation.surface: A diner picks a French dish off the menu, insisting it is beyond doubt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without question!' reads as an emphatic yes, but 'Without' means outside: the anagram of MENU OR COURSE I wraps round Q.
explanation.definitionFit: A croque-monsieur is a toasted ham and cheese sandwich, a classic French café snack.

clue.text: Biscuit's trademark: a climbing plant

definitions.note: the 's stands for is, linking the definition to the wordplay

parts.note: a brand is a trademark

indicators.note: climbing in a down clue means the word goes upwards, so it is reversed

parts.note: a pansy is a garden plant

explanation.surface: A biscuit is branded with a picture of a creeper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'climbing plant' reads as ivy or clematis, but 'climbing' sends PANSY up the grid as YSNAP.
explanation.definitionFit: A brandy snap is a thin, crisp rolled ginger biscuit.

clue.text: Conservative's clever message

parts.note: C is an abbreviation for Conservative
able means clever or capable

explanation.surface: A Tory politician sends a smart communication.
explanation.definitionFit: A cable is a telegram, a message sent by telegraph wire.

clue.text: A lot of bottle shown by Latvian, say, before danger reduced

parts.note: a Latvian is an example of a Balt, from the Baltic states

indicators.note: reduced means cut short, losing its last letter

parts.note: a hazard is a danger

explanation.surface: A Latvian shows plenty of courage ahead of a lessening threat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bottle' is British slang for courage, but here it is a literal wine bottle.
explanation.definitionFit: A balthazar is a huge wine bottle holding sixteen standard bottles, so it is a lot of bottle.

clue.text: Bloomers made in European articles written by don

parts.note: un is a French indefinite article and der a German definite article
der is the German masculine definite article
to don clothes is to wear them

explanation.surface: Women's knickers are produced on the Continent, with pieces penned by a university fellow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'don' suggests an Oxbridge academic, but here it is the verb meaning put on.
explanation.definitionFit: Bloomers are old-fashioned knickers, an example of garments worn beneath one's clothes.

clue.text: Horse fell over end of log in foul place

parts.note: a dun is a greyish-brown horse

indicators.note: end of means the last letter is taken

parts.note: a fell is a hill in northern England

explanation.surface: A horse took a tumble over a log at the edge of a filthy spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fell' looks like the past of fall, but is the northern English word for a hill.
explanation.definitionFit: A dunghill is a heap of manure, a foul and filthy place.

clue.text: PM's term leading a country cut short

definitions.note: the 's stands for is, joining the definition to the wordplay

parts.note: to term something is to call it

indicators.note: cut short means the last letter is removed

parts.note: Ghana is a country in West Africa

explanation.surface: A Prime Minister's time in office leading a nation ends early.
explanation.walkthrough: 'term' looks like a period in office but is the verb to name. James Callaghan was Labour Prime Minister from 1976 to 1979.
explanation.definitionFit: James Callaghan served as British Prime Minister, so his surname answers a request for a PM.

clue.text: In shock about formal dress?

indicators.note: In tells you the about word goes inside the shock word

parts.note: to appal is to shock
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: Someone is horrified by the dress code.
explanation.definitionFit: Apparel is clothing, a formal word for dress.

clue.text: Assume present is a hoax

definitions.meaning: to assume an air or accent is to adopt it falsely
to present a play is to stage it

explanation.surface: Taking something as given amounts to a trick.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means adopt (an accent), stage (a show), and as a noun, a deceptive prank.

clue.text: Coppers lock up bloke losing head as punishment

indicators.note: lock up means enclose, so the coins hold the other piece

parts.note: pence are copper coins

indicators.note: losing head means the first letter goes

parts.note: a man is a bloke

explanation.surface: Police jail a man who has lost his temper as a punishment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coppers' wants to be police, but means copper coins; 'lock up' is the container and 'losing head' trims the bloke.
explanation.definitionFit: Penance is self-imposed suffering to atone for wrongdoing, a kind of punishment.

clue.text: Why punish liar in trouble with judge for outcome of crash?

indicators.note: in trouble suggests the letters are in a mess, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone asks why a lying claimant who had a car accident should be penalised in court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in trouble' turns WHY PUNISH LIAR plus J (judge) into the answer, with the J mixed in.
explanation.definitionFit: A neck injury from sudden jolting is the classic result of a rear-end car collision.

clue.text: One in trouble succeeded for so long abroad

indicators.note: in means the one letter goes inside the trouble word

parts.note: ado means fuss or trouble
one is the Roman numeral I
S is an abbreviation for succeeded, in family trees

explanation.surface: Someone in difficulty gets through, and says goodbye to life overseas.
explanation.definitionFit: Adios is Spanish for goodbye, so it is how they say so long in a foreign land.

clue.text: Speak or talk inaudibly, dropping marks

indicators.note: dropping means a letter is removed

parts.note: to mutter is to speak too low to be heard
M is the abbreviation for marks, the old German currency

explanation.surface: Speaking under one's breath loses points.
explanation.definitionFit: To utter is to say or voice words, to speak.

clue.text: Out of shape, inwardly upset

indicators.note: inwardly upset means the inner letters are overturned, swapping places

parts.note: form means shape

explanation.surface: Someone is out of shape and upset inside.
explanation.walkthrough: The inner OR of FORM is turned over to RO.
explanation.definitionFit: From expresses moving away or out of a place, as in out of the house.

clue.text: Fighting force with men hiding unknown cut-throat

indicators.note: hiding means concealing within, so the army letters enclose the unknown

parts.note: RA is the Royal Artillery
OR, other ranks, means ordinary soldiers
z is an algebraic unknown

explanation.surface: An army unit and its soldiers are concealing a mysterious killer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut-throat' looks like a murderer but is the old open blade used for shaving.
explanation.definitionFit: A cut-throat is a long open blade for shaving, the traditional barber's kind.

clue.text: Single drink not knocked back in part of capital

parts.note: single means one, the Roman numeral I
a sling is a gin-based cocktail

indicators.note: knocked back means reversed, so the word is read the other way

parts.note: taken as written before turning

explanation.surface: A lone drinker refuses to down his glass in London.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knocked back' looks like drinking it down, but turns NOT into TON.
explanation.definitionFit: Islington is a borough of north London, part of Britain's capital city.

clue.text: Painter of frescoes abandoned altruism

indicators.note: abandoned means wild and unrestrained, so the letters run loose

explanation.surface: An artist of wall paintings gave up selflessness.
explanation.definitionFit: A fresco is a painting on wet plaster, so a painter of walls is one who does them.

clue.text: Act without restraint after extremely late visit

indicators.note: after places the trip word behind the late ends
extremely means taking the extremes, the first and last letters

parts.note: a trip is a visit

explanation.surface: Someone goes wild after turning up very late.
explanation.definitionFit: To let rip is to behave freely and unrestrainedly, an informal idiom.
